Paragraph:
Translation: The devotees of the Lord are released from all kinds of sins because they eat food which is offered first for sacrifice. Others, who prepare food for personal sense enjoyment, verily eat only sin.

Purport (Excerpt): ...The santas, being always in a compact of love with the Supreme Personality of Godhead... cannot accept anything without first offering it to the Supreme Person... Others, who prepare food for self or sense gratification, are not only thieves, but are also the eaters of all kinds of sins...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The unconscious consumption of resources driven by selfish desire, which accumulates psychological and spiritual guilt.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna teaches that sanctifying basic daily activities—such as preparing and eating food by offering it to the Lord—frees one from negative reactions (sins), whereas selfish consumption feeds moral and spiritual degradation.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns to turn routine everyday habits into acts of mindfulness and devotion.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Living: Transforming daily routines into conscious, intentional practices
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Sanctifying the Everyday: Elevating basic survival tasks like eating into spiritual acts
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Freedom from Guilt: Clearing the mind of negative emotional remnants tied to selfish action

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Yajna-sistasin (Eating food remnants left after sacrifice/Prasadam)
Bhunjate te tv agham papa (Eating sin by cooking solely for self-indulgence)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Devotees who consume food first offered as a sacrifice (prasadam) are cleansed of all karmic fault. Conversely, those who prepare food purely for self-indulgence internalize sin and remain bound to material suffering.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: How we engage with everyday habits impacts our internal state. Approaching basic acts like eating with mindfulness, gratitude, and a spirit of sharing purifies the mind. Self-centered indulgence breeds internal conflict, whereas intentional, sanctified living brings inner peace.
